## [`Docs/Plans/ImplementationPlan-Network.md`](../Plans/ImplementationPlan-Network.md)

| Gate | Decision | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | **The links a change is measured over, and what it is held to.** Proposed, three profiles of `ImpairedLink`, each way: *near*, a 20 ms round trip, ±5 ms of jitter and 0.1% loss; *Wi-Fi*, 40 ms, ±15 ms and 1%; *hotspot*, 80 ms, ±30 ms, 2%, and 4 Mbit/s to the client, below the snapshot rate under load (§1 finding 4). Proposed targets, to be rows of [the budgets](../Budgets.md) once NW2 has measured against them: on every profile, no more than two ticks of a seat's state waiting on the server; the newest state a client holds more than two ticks behind the server in at most 1% of samples on near and Wi-Fi, and 5% on hotspot; an order's response at most 150 ms plus the link's round trip, at the 95th percentile; and no target for bandwidth, which F5 has measured, not held. | NW2.2 and NW2.3, and whether NW3 and NW4 go ahead |
| M2 | **The version of a changed protocol.** F5 has deltas or datagrams come "as a new protocol version", while `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 1 until the game is live (AGENTS.md R18; owner, 2026-10-09) and the layout's hash refuses a game of another build (ADR-060 decision 5). Proposed: until the game is live, a change to the messages is told by the hash alone, and F5's new version is read as that. | NW3.1 |
| M3 | **What crosses once.** Proposed: on the wire only, so that `Snapshot` stays what every reader reads: the client, the AI, a deputy, the match log and the universe log. The server's end of a QUIC seat keeps the catalogue it last sent that seat (the hulls, drives, weapons, modules, research topics, designs and structure types as the player's research has them, the sectors' names and borders, the map's size, the Constructor's cost and time, the tickets and their drain, and the asteroid fields), and sends it whole when the seat is taken and before the snapshot of any tick in which it changed; the snapshot on the wire leaves it out. `QuicTransport` keeps the last catalogue and puts it back, so that every snapshot it hands on is the snapshot the server built. The server finds a change by comparing, so `Simulation` holds nothing new (AGENTS.md R18). The sectors' holders, suppression, cut-off and guard stay in the snapshot, and so do the ore asteroids, whose reserves change as they are mined. | NW3.1 |
| M4 | **The streams.** Proposed: commands go up the bidirectional stream the client opens, as now, and each tick's shots, destructions, events and report of a time away come down it, reliably and in order. Each tick's state comes down a unidirectional stream of its own, which the server opens and ends with the state. When the server sends a seat a state, it aborts every older state stream of that seat not yet acknowledged, so that a seat has only the newest state on its way and no backlog; an abort loses only a state not yet whole at the client. The events go first when both have something to send. `QuicTransport` hands on a snapshot for each state it receives, with the events of every tick since the last it handed on, each shot and destruction carrying its tick, so that an explosion still plays where it happened. The alternatives: QUIC datagrams for state, which at 1,200 bytes would have to be cut up and put back together, reliability written by hand under another name; and one stream on which state is skipped while a seat's backlog is over a snapshot, which bounds memory and latency in a day's work but keeps the stall of finding 1. | NW4.1 |
| M5 | **The view's delay.** Proposed: the view runs behind the newest state by what the link needs rather than by one tick: by how late states have arrived over the last 10 s, at their 95th percentile, at least 1 tick and at most 4, 200 ms at 20 Hz. Its clock follows the server's ticks, as an offset from the frame's clock smoothed over many arrivals, rather than the arrival of the newest. It still never extrapolates. On the loopback it stays at 1 tick, so a skirmish shows what it shows now. | NW5.1 |
| M6 | **The order's mark.** Proposed: as the player gives a move, an attack-move, a hold of a sector or a patrol, its point is marked on the ground at once, and an attack's target, by a ring in the color of the selection's ring (ADR-067) that shrinks to nothing over 0.4 s; a refusal of that order (gate M7) turns its mark the warning color (ADR-085 decision 1). It predicts nothing: the ships move when a snapshot says they do. | NW6.1 |
| M7 | **A command's number.** Proposed: the client numbers its commands, and a refusal names the number of the command it refuses (ADR-094 decision 1); the server trusts the number for nothing (ADR-002 decision 2). The order's mark reads it now (gate M6), and an acknowledgement or a prediction would need it later (gate M11). `EventView` carries it, so the layout of what a universe saves changes and version 1's hash is replaced (AGENTS.md R18), with what that does to a running universe, as the milestone order says. | NW3.2 |
| M8 | **A universe's lost connection.** Proposed: in a universe, a connection lost for any reason but the server's own close (`Finished`, `WrongVersion`, `SeatRefused` or `SeatTaken`), or silent for 10 s, is joined again with the same join file, at once and then every 2 s for 30 s, while the match stays on screen and the tag says "Reconnecting · 5 s"; after that, the menu, as now. 30 s is half the deputy's minute, so a link that drops for a moment never hands the seat to the deputy (ADR-079 decision 4). A skirmish, whose server is in the game, goes back to the menu as now. | NW6.2 |
| M9 | **A seat's commands.** Proposed: a seated client's message is at most 64 KiB, which holds a command naming every ship a fleet cap allows many times over; a seat's commands are applied at most 32 a tick, and the rest wait for the next tick, in the order given; and a connection with more than 1,200 waiting, nearly two seconds behind at 32 a tick, is closed as `MalformedMessage`. Every connection is held to them, the loopback's and the hosted players' too, so that what the tests play is what a match plays; NW1.3 shows that no AI meets them. | NW1.3 |
| M10 | **The round trip on the tag.** Proposed: in a universe the tag gives the connection's smoothed round trip beside the address, in whole milliseconds, "Server 203.0.113.5:4433 · 42 ms"; a skirmish's tag stays "Local skirmish". It lifts ADR-086's foreclosure of a round trip on the tag. | NW6.3 |
| M11 | **Acknowledgement or prediction** (ADR-002 decision 5), from NW6.4's measurement over a real network. Proposed: neither, while the order's mark and the measured response hold gate M1's target; if the response misses it, which of the two is a plan of its own. | A later plan, if any |
